expectations.text: Measured per-test durations across the whole suite
expectations.evidence: 'Ran pytest --durations=0 to get a full per-test timing breakdown before touching anything, rather than guessing'.

expectations.text: Distinguished the single hotspot from the uniform per-test tax as different problems
expectations.evidence: 'Two independent issues' — a 5.67s quadratic and a ~2.5s fixture sleep across 39 tests, reported separately.

expectations.text: Reported concentration — how few files hold most of the wall-clock
expectations.evidence: 68% in one test, 30% in the api_client fixture.

expectations.text: Reported that 12 tests are silently skipped
expectations.evidence: 'test_legacy.py ... is skipif'd out on darwin/linux, so it never paid this cost either way (the 12 skips seen in the run were that file)' — framed purely as a timing exclusion.

expectations.text: Gave a prioritised order with the hotspot first, rather than an undifferentiated list
expectations.evidence: Numbered findings with the 68% quadratic first.

needs_review: RUBRIC BLIND SPOT: this arm's fix does not remove the quadratic. A scaling probe of its FakeLedger gives 6k/12k/24k ratios of 3.94, 3.78 — still O(n^2). It bought a ~15x constant factor (per-account bucketing plus C-level sum) and reported '18x faster, 94.5% reduction'. No assertion in eval-2 can see this, so it scores the same as the with_skill arm, which is LINEAR (1.47, 2.44).
